candidate.title: From Reflection to Action: 8 Hot Takes from CC’s Open Heritage Roundtable
candidate.accessNote: Somente metadados do feed; página original não foi consultada. Na ausência de idioma declarado, a inferência conservadora usa apenas o título.

evidence: From Exploratory Dialogue to Roundtable At our Open Heritage Dialogue held at UNESCO House last April, we had convened to find answers to an important question: How can equitable access to heritage help solve global challenges? What we heard was that it can in a diversity of ways: from supporting access to education to strengthening social inclusion and spurring artistic creativity, all the way to helping find concrete solutions to fight climate change. Five months later, on 29 September, we returned to Paris ready to move the conversation forward. Together with the Representation of Québec within the Permanent Delegation of Canada to UNESCO, we brought together around 30 participants to our Open Heritage Roundtable to discuss possible ways forward at UNESCO, with whom CC is an NGO in official partnership (consultative status) . Participants hailed from UNESCO permanent delegations, UNESCO national commissions, national government and ministries of culture, national libraries and archives, international NGOs from the open heritage community, including the Open Heritage Coalition, among others, and their interventions were made in French and English.
